successors.name: Principality of Hungary
successors.text: the tribal territories east of the Principality's core, 'the domains of Gyula the Younger in Transylvania' and the lands of the other tribes

ledger.x: c. 840: the Magyars settle the Etelköz, between the Carpathians and the Dnieper. The Hungarians page: 'Around 830, a rebellion broke out in the Khazar khaganate' and the Hungarians moved to 'the Etelköz, the territory between the Carpathians and the Dnieper River'; the Etelköz page puts the exodus from Levedia 'around…
884: Cliopatria's Magyars shape shrinks by 14,668 km2 while its Kievan Rus' shape grows into the same cells.
By 892: the Pechenegs drive the Magyars west of the Dnieper.

c. 895: a Pecheneg invasion drives the Magyars out of Etelköz. 'A new Pecheneg invasion compelled the Magyars to leave Etelköz and cross the Carpathian Mountains around 895.' The Hungarian conquest page: 'a joint attack by the Pechenegs and Bulgarians in 894 or 895'; the Pechenegs page: they 'drove out the Magyars…
895/896: under Árpád the Hungarians cross the Carpathians into the Basin.
Cliopatria 896-897: the Magyars hold the lower Dniester steppe.
896: the Hungarians enter land that Cliopatria's Great Moravia shape holds to 895.
900: the Hungarian core is drawn as the Principality of Hungary.
900: a fringe of the Carpathian side drops out of the shape.

c. 907: the tribal confederation becomes the single Principality under Árpád and his heirs. The Principality page: 'After Kurszán's death this division ceased and Árpád became the sole ruler'; the kende rule ends 'c. 904' or 907 (text); Kurszán's death is dated 902 or 904. Gyula's…
907: the Magyar row ends; the land continues under the Principality of Hungary. Árpád's rule is 'c.

wars.name: Pecheneg drive-out of the Magyars from Etelköz
wars.outcome: The Pechenegs, 'Driven further west by the Khazars and Cumans by 889', 'drove the Magyars west of the Dnieper River by 892' and then 'drove out the Magyars remaining in Etelköz'; Simeon I of Bulgaria 'employed the Pechenegs to help fend off the Magyars'…

wars.name: Hungarian-Bulgarian war of 894-896
wars.outcome: The Byzantines invaded Bulgaria from the south as the Hungarians attacked from the north; Simeon fled to Dristra; 'The Bulgarians ... attacked and routed the Hungarians'.

wars.name: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin
wars.outcome: The Hungarians crossed the Carpathians in 895/896, took Pannonia in 900, defeated Great Moravia in 902 and beat the Bavarians at Pressburg on 4 July 907; the tribal territories east of the core stayed semi-independent.

certainty.note: A nomadic confederation's range: the Etelköz is described by rivers (Dnieper, Dniester, Prut, Siret) and the Muslim sources by two others; no frontier is fixed on any page.
